jobs.title: Business Consultant
jobs.description:
About Us
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Job Summary

The Business Consultant, Business Strategy & Operations, serves as a seasoned individual contributor responsible for solving complex operational problems with designated clients. This role takes a broad perspective to identify operational performance improvement opportunities and supports the adoption of innovative solutions. The consultant acts as a functional specialist, focusing on building and extending client relationships, and works independently with limited supervision except in the most complex situations. The position requires proactive identification of processing efficiencies, support for service changes, and system enhancements, while maintaining strong knowledge of Visa products and services.

All roles require digital fluency, including the ability to work with emerging technologies such as Generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot) to support everyday work.

Key Responsibilities:

- Own the CMS business reviews, including deliverables, stakeholder coordination, and timeline execution.
- Develop executive-ready presentations that highlight business performance, strategic priorities, risks, opportunities, and key decisions.
- Synthesis inputs across Visa Direct, VCS, and VGS, by working with Sales, Finance and Operations teams.
- Enhance reporting frameworks to focus leadership discussions on forward-looking insights, performance gaps, strategic trade-offs, and actionable decisions rather than status reporting.
- Maintain action-item governance and follow-through from business reviews.
- Partner with Finance and business leaders to monitor revenue and expense performance against AOP and forecast.
- Develop and maintain long-terim revenue forecasts and performance models.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

- 5 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelors Degree or at least 2 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 0 years of work experience with a PhD

Preferred Qualifications:

- 6 or more years of work experience with a Bachelors Degree or 4 or more years of relevant experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA,  JD, MD) or up to 3 years of relevant experience with a PhD
- 5 or more years of of experience in business management, finance, strategy, sales operations, management consulting, or related analytical roles.
- Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business performance management experience.
- Experience developing executive-level presentations and leadership communications.
- Advanced analytical skills with expertise in Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to synthesize large datasets into executive insights and recommendations.
- Proven ability to influence stakeholders across multiple organizations without direct authority.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Experience supporting executive leadership teams.
- Experience with performance reporting, MBR/QBR processes, and operating reviews.
- Familiarity with revenue forecasting, P&L management, budgeting, and financial planning.
- Experience using Power BI, Tableau, AI Tools or other analytics platforms.

Information for US Applicants
For roles located in the US, the estimated salary range for this position is $136,000.00 to $ 217,000.00 USD per year, which may include potential sales incentive payments (if applicable). Salary may vary depending on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location. In addition, this position may be eligible for bonus and equity.Visa has a comprehensive benefits package for which this position may be eligible that includes Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), FSA/HSA, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, and Wellness Program.
Work Hours
Varies upon the needs of the department.

Travel Requirements
This position requires travel 5-10% of the time.

Mental/Physical Requirements
This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, frequently operate standard office equipment, such as telephones and computers.

Visa is an EEO Employer
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protect veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the EEOC guidelines and applicable local law, including the requirements of Article 49 of the San Francisco Police Code.

jobs.description:
About Us
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Visa’s Asia Pacific Corporate Strategy team based in Singapore plays a key role in shaping Visa’s long-term strategy in the region and solving for regional and country-specific opportunities and challenges, in partnership with executives and business leaders across Visa’s organization. Recent initiatives have addressed topics such as market strategy, product strategy, multi-year planning, and organic / inorganic growth opportunities across the region. The team is also responsible for developing thought leadership on emerging trends in payments industry.

What a Senior Director of Corporate Strategy does at Visa:
The Senior Director will be a member of Visa's AP Corporate Strategy team, which is responsible for development of regional and market-specific strategy efforts. As a strategist, the individual will work with and support key areas of the business – both across functions and geographies – in conducting analysis to support development of strategies in alignment with the regional and global priorities. This role will also support regional business planning needs, monitoring of competitive developments across the region / globally, and development of timely response to emerging trends and opportunities across AP. The position will be based in Singapore with some travel expected.

This Senior Director role in the AP Corporate Strategy team supports the AP Regional Head of Strategy in the formulation, analytical review, preparation and communication of the AP strategy and associated Sub Regional and Market Strategy plans. A typical effort may entail working closely with senior stakeholders to understand and logically structure the problem, develop hypothesis, work with cross-functional teams to validate the hypothesis, develop strategy to address the problem, and develop recommendations and execution plan to present to the AP Regional President and the leadership team. The Senior Director is expected to lead end-to-end strategy efforts independently or with a small team of analysts depending on the scope and complexity of the effort. The strategy efforts can range from developing country strategies to developing multi-year plans for the region, addressing emerging competitive and economic model issues, managing commercial response to regulatory changes, developing go-to-market plans for new solutions, and supporting strategic investment assessments.

Why this is important to Visa:
The AP Corporate Strategy team is responsible for helping the senior leadership team in setting the strategic agenda for Visa in AP in close alignment with the Global Corporate Strategy. In close alignment with the regional and global leadership team, you will be instrumental in defining, planning and executing long-term strategic priorities that will set Visa (encompassing all our segments, channels and geographies) on a path to create even greater value for Visa’s shareholders.

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

What you will need for this role:
We are looking for an individual with a structured mindset, curiosity about the payments industry, is results-driven, and client focused. As an ideal candidate, you should have:
- Bachelor or Master’s degree preferably in Economics, Business or similar fields
- 15+ years of experience in leading strategy projects at top-tier Management Consulting firms or in a Corporate Strategy group in a multinational environment
- Pro-active and effective communicator, experienced in presenting information to all levels and with ability to facilitate group discussions and debate
- Ability to lead cross-functional teams and proven experience of project management
- Strong interpersonal and execution skills
- Strong analytical and strategic acumen
- Excellent presentation and verbal and written communication skills
- Able to manage work in different time zones effectively
- Ability to be recognized as thought leader
- Ability to influence the organization in order to make strategy happen
- Professional, confident and outgoing with the ability to maintain good communication with wide internal and external audiences
- Team player possessing a strong drive to add value to the business direction
- Highly numerate with attention to detail and ability to structure and analyze databases and strong knowledge of financial modelling, scenario-building and analysis

What will also help:
- Financial Services / FinTech / Payment industry experience would be a distinct advantage
- Broad understanding / experience in financial services and / or payments a plus

Visa is an EEO Employer
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

Job Description

The Director, Strategy & Business Operations will serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to the SVP, Platform Products. The role will help the Platform Products Leadership Team develop, communicate, and execute its strategy, translate priorities into measurable outcomes, and maintain alignment across a complex global portfolio.

This role combines strategic planning, business operations, executive communications, and cross-functional execution. The Director will support the articulation of the Platform Products strategy, organize structured deep dives with initiative owners, establish a disciplined operating rhythm, and provide clear, data-driven updates to senior leaders.
Working across Product, Technology, Design, Finance, People, and regional teams, the Director will help connect Visa's enterprise priorities to execution while advancing practical, AI-enabled ways of working that improve the quality and speed of planning, analysis, and communication.

Strategic Planning & Execution
- Partner with the SVP and Platform Products Leadership Team to develop, refine, and communicate the organization’s strategy and priorities.
- Ensure strategic priorities are clearly linked to evidenced client needs, business outcomes, and Visa’s enterprise objectives.
- Translate strategy into a focused set of outcomes, measures, and actions, with clear ownership and follow-through.

Strategy Deep Dives
- Design and facilitate structured deep dives on the organization’s most important strategic initiatives.
- Partner with initiative owners to define the questions to resolve, assemble relevant facts, and develop clear options and recommendations.
- Ensure reviews focus on client and business outcomes, strategic choices, execution confidence, dependencies, and decisions rather than activity reporting.
- Synthesize discussions into clear decisions, actions, owners, and follow-up.

Executive Updates & Communications
- Establish a regular cadence of concise executive updates covering progress against outcomes, material risks, key decisions, and areas requiring intervention.
- Develop high-quality narratives, briefing materials, and presentations for senior leadership forums, business reviews, town halls, and other critical organizational moments.
- Translate complex product, platform, and technology topics into clear, decision-oriented communications for varied audiences.
- Support leadership messaging that strengthens organizational clarity, alignment, and engagement.

Business Management & Operating Rhythm
- Lead key business management cadences, including strategy reviews, quarterly business reviews, OKR reviews, leadership meetings, off-sites, and planning processes.

- Drive follow-through on leadership decisions and time-sensitive deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and completion.
- Continuously simplify processes, eliminate low-value activity, and improve organizational effectiveness.

AI-Enabled Ways of Working
- Identify and apply AI-enabled tools and practices that improve strategy development, synthesis, planning, reporting, and executive communications.
- Help initiative owners and leadership teams adopt practical new ways of working that increase productivity and decision quality.
- Partner across Product and Technology to share effective practices and demonstrate measurable value from adoption.

Cross-Functional Partnership
- Build strong working relationships across Product, Technology, Design, Finance, People, regional teams, and other Visa functions.
- Bring together the right stakeholders to resolve cross-functional issues and maintain alignment on strategic priorities.
- Act as a trusted point of coordination for matters requiring SVP or Leadership Team attention.

- The Platform Products strategy is clear, repeatable, and consistently connected to client and business outcomes.
- Strategy deep dives result in sharper choices, timely decisions, named owners, and clear next steps.
- Senior leaders receive concise, candid, and decision-oriented updates with early visibility into material risks and dependencies.
- Planning and business management cadences improve focus, alignment, and execution without adding unnecessary process.

Preferred Qualifications
- 12 or more years of work experience with a   Bachelor’s Degree   or 8-10 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 6+ years of work experience with a PhD
- Demonstrated experience partnering with senior executives and preparing clear, decision-quality narratives and recommendations.
- Experience leading strategic planning, business reviews, and complex cross-functional initiatives in a global or matrixed organization.
- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information for executive audiences.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, including the judgment to distinguish material issues from routine execution detail.
- Ability to influence across organizational boundaries, challenge constructively, and drive outcomes without direct authority.
- Experience with digital platforms, payments, product development, or scaled technology environments is preferred.
- Practical experience using AI-enabled tools to improve analysis, planning, communication, or team productivity is preferred.

Leadership Profile
- A strategic operator who can connect direction, execution, and measurable business outcomes.
- An exceptional communicator who brings clarity to ambiguity and complexity.
- A rigorous facilitator who asks incisive questions and helps leaders sharpen options and recommendations.
- A collaborative partner who builds trust, exercises sound judgment, and works effectively across functions and regions.

- Develop toolkits, guidance materials and playbooks that support adoption and organisational change.

Digital, AI & Platform Adoption
- Support the deployment and adoption of digital platforms, knowledge ecosystems and AI-enabled capabilities across VCA Europe.

This incumbent will help establish the operating disciplines, planning processes, governance mechanisms, and delivery-management practices required to support VCA-X. - Establish and continuously improve the delivery lifecycle, governance mechanisms, decision rights, and operating disciplines required to support VCA-X at scale.

- Drive continuous improvement through operational learning, performance data, and delivery insights.

- Support prioritization and investment decisions by providing visibility into delivery feasibility, trade-offs, and resource implications.

- Orchestrate integrated capacity planning and staffing coordination across Specialist, Consulting, Analytics, and Engineering teams.

- Coordinate resolution of issues requiring alignment across teams, functions, or geographies.

- Establish performance measures and management routines that improve predictability, throughput, and scalability.

- Drive improvements that reduce delivery friction and improve operational efficiency.

- Provide leadership with clear visibility into commitments, constraints, decisions, and required interventions.

- Support the management of external delivery and specialist partners that augment VCA-X capacity, accelerate capability development, and support efficient scaling across Regions and use cases.

- Foster alignment across a highly matrixed global organization.

Team & Organizational Leadership:
- Support and help build a high-performing Program Management organization.

- Establish career paths, capabilities, and leadership expectations for program management professionals.

- Contribute to the overall strategy, culture, and success of the VCA-X leadership team.

- Demonstrated success building and operating delivery organizations in complex, matrixed, global environments.
- Experience managing large portfolios involving multiple stakeholders, disciplines, geographies, and competing priorities.

The Risk Management Director serves as Head of Risk for the Eastern Africa cluster, with primary accountability for protecting and strengthening the payments ecosystem while enabling responsible business growth across a diverse set of markets, clients, regulators and payment use cases.
The role holder leads end-to-end risk engagement across Eastern Africa with Visa clients, partners, merchants, fintechs, regulators and internal stakeholders. The role covers all relevant risk dimensions, including fraud, scams, cybersecurity, data security, ecosystem integrity, credit and settlement risk, third-party risk, regulatory risk, AML/sanctions considerations, emerging technologies, cross-border flows, mobile-first digital payments and new money movement models.

Externally, the Risk Director ensures Visa’s interactions with clients, merchants, regulators, law enforcement, government agencies, mobile money operators, fintechs and other ecosystem participants across Eastern Africa are well informed, constructive and focused on building digital trust, strengthening resilience, advancing financial inclusion and supporting secure growth.
Internally, the Risk Director translates market intelligence into actionable insights that influence Visa’s strategy, products, policies, controls and client solutions. The role partners across business, product, legal, compliance, government engagement, technology, operations and regional risk teams to ensure risk management is embedded early in commercial and innovation decisions.

The role combines traditional risk management disciplines with the capabilities required of a modern payments risk leader: ecosystem intelligence, data-driven decision-making, AI and fraud analytics fluency, regulatory credibility, commercial judgment, crisis leadership and the ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.

Success in the role is measured by the ability to reduce risk, build trust, enable growth, strengthen client and regulatory relationships, enhance Visa’s reputation, and improve ecosystem outcomes through proactive prevention, effective response and sustained stakeholder engagement.
The Risk Director will also help strengthen Visa shareholder value by improving information flow around strategic, regulatory, operational and emerging risks; supporting disciplined execution of risk programs; and minimizing audit, compliance, operational and reputational concerns.

Principle Responsibilities/Key Results Area:
Six core principles provide the foundation for modern risk management at Visa:
- Market and ecosystem intelligence: Maintain a deep understanding of the business environment, regulatory expectations, client capabilities, payment flows, fraud typologies, cyber and scam trends, third-party dependencies and emerging risks across each market.
- Growth with control: Align risk priorities with Visa’s commercial strategy by helping clients, partners and internal teams grow responsibly, launch safely and make risk-informed decisions early.
- Digital trust and resilience: Strengthen ecosystem confidence through prevention, monitoring, response, recovery and control maturity across fraud, scams, data security, cybersecurity, credit settlement and operational risk.
- Stakeholder influence: Engage clients, merchants, fintechs, regulators, law enforcement, government and internal partners to secure alignment, shape outcomes and address identified risks.
- Thought leadership: Differentiate Visa by translating local, regional and global intelligence into practical insights, risk strategies, client advisory, industry education and policy engagement.
- Clear communication and accountability: Provide timely marketplace feedback, executive-level updates, risk reporting, escalation and transparent communication on programs, policies, incidents and outcomes.
- Eastern Africa Risk Intelligence and Strategy: Maintain an informed view of Eastern Africa market dynamics, regulatory expectations, client capabilities, mobile-first payment flows, cross-border corridors, fraud typologies, cyber and scam trends, third-party dependencies and emerging risks. Translate this intelligence into cluster-level priorities that protect Visa and enable secure growth.
- Business Enablement and Risk-Based Growth: Partner with business, product and client teams to embed risk assessment early in market expansion, product launches, new partnerships, fintech engagement, merchant acquiring, digital acceptance, Visa Pay, mobile money-linked use cases, remittances, commercial payments and emerging money movement flows. Support growth by identifying practical controls, governance expectations and remediation pathways.
- Fraud, Scam and Digital Trust Leadership: Lead Eastern Africa engagement on fraud prevention, scam disruption, authentication, tokenization, dispute and chargeback trends, account-to-account risks, AI-enabled threats and customer protection. Use data, analytics and Visa risk capabilities to identify opportunities that improve authorization performance, reduce losses and strengthen trust.
- Regulatory, Government and Industry Engagement : Serve as a credible risk point of contact for central banks, regulators, government agencies, law enforcement and industry bodies across the cluster. Provide input on policy developments, regulatory inquiries, supervisory engagements and market initiatives affecting payment security, consumer protection, AML expectations, data integrity, cyber resilience and financial inclusion.
- Client, Fintech and Partner Advisory : Be the primary Visa risk advisor to key issuers, acquirers, fintechs, mobile money operators, merchants and payment ecosystem stakeholders. Develop and execute structured engagement plans, executive risk reviews, risk councils, training sessions and targeted remediation support to strengthen client controls and performance.
- Credit, Settlement and Financial Risk Oversight: Support in-market credit and settlement risk management by monitoring client financial health, settlement exposure, collateral requirements, risk triggers and escalation needs. Partner with regional and global teams on high-risk clients, below-investment-grade exposure, remediation, approvals and governance.
- Incident, Crisis and Issue Management: Coordinate timely response to significant fraud events, data compromise incidents, ecosystem integrity matters, regulatory escalations and client control failures across the cluster. Ensure clear ownership, escalation, communication, lessons learned and sustainable remediation.
- Governance, Reporting and Communication : Provide concise executive updates, risk dashboards, marketplace feedback and issue reporting to internal stakeholders. Ensure cluster priorities align with Visa policies, programs, audit expectations, enterprise risk management frameworks and regional objectives for Sub-Saharan Africa.

The role is a trusted, practical and risk-based partner to business and control functions, helping ensure sound decision-making, effective controls and consistent application of Visa policies, international standards and applicable legal and regulatory requirements. The position has a strong day-to-day focus on AML/ATF and sanctions risk while supporting the wider ethics and compliance framework.

Key risk areas

- Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing (AML/ATF)
- Sanctions, including Office of Foreign Assets Control requirements and other applicable sanctions regimes
- Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
- Business conduct and ethics, conflicts of interest and prevention of insider trading
- Data privacy, information security, competition law and other applicable regulatory requirements

Core responsibilities

- Provide practical, risk-based advice on business initiatives, products, client engagements and transactions, and support the design and execution of proportionate mitigation actions.
- Support regulatory engagement on AML/ATF and other compliance matters in collaboration with Legal, Government Affairs and regional Ethics & Compliance leadership.
- Provide compliance input and coordination support for engagements with relevant financial, payments, data-protection and other governmental authorities in Uzbekistan.
- Collaborate with Visa financial intelligence and specialist teams on enhanced due diligence, AML/ATF and sanctions reviews, including client information requests and follow-up actions.

- Execute AML/ATF, sanctions and anti-bribery due diligence, including third-party reviews, client education, workshops and client programme assessments.
- Support regulatory reporting and compliance submissions, ensuring that inputs are accurate, complete, timely and appropriately escalated.
- Promote awareness of the Ethics & Compliance Program and Code of Business Conduct and Ethics through training, communications and office or market engagement.
- Support internal reviews and investigations where required, maintaining appropriate confidentiality, documentation and escalation.
- Track emerging regulatory, financial-crime and payments-industry developments and translate relevant changes into practical business guidance.
- Maintain effective records, management information and reporting on compliance risks, reviews, remediation and programme activities.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent higher-education qualification in law, finance, business, risk, compliance or a related discipline.
- Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in ethics and compliance, AML/ATF, sanctions, financial crime, risk management or controls within financial services, payments or regulated technology.

- Good understanding of payments products, emerging payment technologies and relevant regulatory developments.

- Strong analytical and data-handling skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint and related applications.

Core capabilities

- High integrity and sound judgement, with the confidence to question, challenge and escalate when required.
- Clear, professional written, presentation and communication skills.
- Able to translate regulatory expectations into practical, commercially aware guidance.
- Collaborative and credible with stakeholders at different levels, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
- Self-motivated, organised and able to manage competing priorities with limited supervision in a dispersed team.
- Adaptable and comfortable working across cultures, time zones and evolving business needs.

This role may operate in a hybrid environment, subject to local site and leadership requirements. Periodic travel and participation in calls outside standard local business hours may be required to support regional and global stakeholders.

- Effective identification, escalation and mitigation of material compliance risks.

The person will support the Principal Officer in ensuring that Visa’s GIFT City activities are conducted in accordance with applicable IFSCA requirements, internal Visa policies, risk and control standards, and the scope of the entity’s ancillary license.

At the same time, the individual will be responsible for ensuring that GIFT City clients — including banks, payment service providers, fintechs, financial institutions, and other eligible entities — receive high-quality client support across onboarding, implementation, issue resolution, operational readiness, reporting, service reviews, and ongoing relationship servicing.

This role will be critical in building a strong control environment while enabling a seamless client experience for Visa’s GIFT City business.

What the Compliance Officer & Senior Manager, Client Services Will Do:
Compliance Officer for Visa GIFT City Entity:
- Serve as Visa’s designated Compliance Officer for its IFSCA-licensed GIFT City entity.
- Support the Principal Officer in maintaining ongoing compliance with applicable IFSCA regulations, circulars, guidelines, license conditions, and internal governance standards.
- Monitor the GIFT City entity’s activities to ensure they remain within the approved scope of Visa’s ancillary license.
- Maintain a compliance calendar covering applicable regulatory filings, submissions, periodic reporting, renewals, certifications, governance reviews, and internal deliverables.
- Coordinate with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Regulatory Affairs, Finance, Tax, Operations, and Client Services teams to ensure regulatory obligations are understood, assigned, tracked, and completed on time.
- Assist in preparing responses to IFSCA information requests, regulatory inspections, supervisory reviews, internal audits, compliance testing, and governance reviews.
- Ensure accurate maintenance of compliance documentation, records, approvals, licenses, policies, SOPs, client records, filings, and audit evidence.
- Track changes in applicable regulations and coordinate with relevant internal stakeholders to assess impact on Visa’s GIFT City activities.
- Support regulatory change management by helping translate legal and regulatory requirements into operational procedures, controls, checklists, and staff awareness materials.
- Escalate actual or potential compliance breaches, regulatory issues, control gaps, conflicts, and operational risks in a timely and structured manner.
- Help build and maintain a culture of compliance, accountability, documentation discipline, and ethical business conduct across the GIFT City office.

Client Services Leadership for GIFT City Clients:
- Lead client services delivery for all Visa GIFT City clients, including banks, payment service providers, fintechs, financial institutions, and other approved or eligible clients.
- Act as the primary senior client services contact for GIFT City clients, ensuring a consistent, responsive, and high-quality client experience.
- Own operational readiness, implementation coordination, client onboarding support, issue resolution, service reviews, and ongoing client engagement from a servicing perspective.
- Partner with Sales, Product, Technology, Risk, Legal, Finance, Client Implementation, and regional Client Services teams to deliver Visa solutions efficiently and effectively.
- Help clients understand Visa processes, operating requirements, service models, implementation timelines, documentation needs, support channels, and escalation protocols.
- Manage complex client service issues, ensuring timely triage, internal ownership, root-cause analysis, escalation, resolution, and client communication.
- Monitor service performance, client satisfaction, open issues, implementation milestones, operational risks, and service-level trends.
- Conduct periodic client service reviews to discuss operational performance, upcoming initiatives, pain points, risk items, product adoption, and improvement opportunities.
- Serve as the consolidated voice of GIFT City clients for service experience, operational feedback, product usability, process friction, reporting needs, and implementation challenges.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives to simplify client onboarding, reduce service issues, enhance operational transparency, and improve client satisfaction.

Regulatory, Risk & Control Ownership:
- Support strong risk and control discipline across Visa’s GIFT City operations.
- Ensure Client Services activities are aligned with applicable compliance requirements, internal controls, policies, and risk standards.
- Coordinate with Risk and Compliance stakeholders to provide accurate, timely, and consolidated business inputs across clients, consistent with the governance discipline described in the source JD.
- Own documentation standards, audit readiness, and governance discipline for Compliance and Client Services outputs, consistent with the source JD’s emphasis on documentation, audit readiness, and control ownership.
- Maintain structured evidence for client onboarding, implementation approvals, client communications, issue escalations, service reviews, and regulatory-relevant activities.
- Identify potential operational, compliance, client, reputational, or regulatory risks and coordinate appropriate remediation plans.
- Help establish and maintain standard operating procedures, checklists, controls, and review mechanisms for GIFT City client servicing.
- Participate in internal risk assessments, control reviews, audits, compliance monitoring, and remediation activities.
- Ensure client-related issues with regulatory or compliance implications are escalated promptly to the Principal Officer & and appropriate internal teams.

Client Onboarding, Implementation & Operational Readiness:
- Coordinate onboarding of new GIFT City clients onto Visa products, services, platforms, and operating processes.
- Ensure client implementation plans are clearly documented, agreed, tracked, and governed.
- Partner with Implementation, Product, Technology, Risk, Legal, Finance, and Sales teams to support timely launch of client programs.
- Help manage dependencies related to contracts, technical setup, testing, certifications, documentation, billing setup, operational procedures, and go-live readiness.
- Ensure clients are appropriately educated on operational responsibilities, compliance requirements, processing flows, reporting processes, and service channels.
- Track implementation risks, blockers, delays, dependencies, and escalations.
- Provide regular updates to the Principal Officer, Sales leads, Client Services leadership, and other stakeholders on client implementation status.
- Support post-launch stabilization, early-life support, issue triage, and transition to business-as-usual servicing.

Issue Management, Escalations & Service Excellence:
- Own the end-to-end coordination of client service issues for GIFT City clients.

- Ensure each issue has clear ownership, severity classification, resolution timeline, client communication plan, and closure evidence.
- Partner with regional and global Visa support teams to resolve complex client issues.

- Drive service excellence by improving responsiveness, transparency, accountability, and follow-through.

Business Operations, Reporting & Governance:
- Build and maintain operational dashboards for GIFT City client services, compliance actions, regulatory deliverables, implementation milestones, and issue management.
- Deliver timely, accurate, and actionable updates to the Principal Officer and senior stakeholders.
- Translate client service data, compliance status, and operational trends into clear recommendations and management insights.
- Support strategic initiatives related to service model design, operational readiness, client support infrastructure, regulatory reporting, and process improvement.

- Contribute to governance forums including branch operating reviews, client review meetings, compliance reviews, risk/control reviews, and management updates.
- Maintain clear minutes, action logs, decisions, approvals, and evidence for governance meetings.
- Drive consistent use of internal tools for issue tracking, client documentation, implementation tracking, CRM updates, reporting, and operational workflows.

Sales, Product & Cross-Functional Partnership:
- Partner closely with the Principal Officer and Sales teams to support client growth through strong service delivery and operational execution.
- Provide client services input during deal planning, solution design, implementation planning, contract discussions, and client readiness assessments.
- Help identify operational dependencies, client requirements, product limitations, service risks, and implementation complexity early in the sales cycle.
- Work with Product and Solutions teams to provide structured feedback from GIFT City clients on Visa products, implementation requirements, service needs, and market expectations.
- Build strong partnerships across Sales, Finance, Product, Strategy, Risk, Legal, HR, and Client Services, consistent with the source JD’s stakeholder management expectations.
- Support client workshops, onboarding sessions, implementation reviews, service reviews, and operating model discussions.
- Ensure that service commitments are realistic, documented, aligned with Visa capabilities, and operationally executable.

Key Measures of Success:
- Regulatory compliance - Timely filings, no material compliance breaches, strong audit outcomes, complete regulatory records
- License governance - Activities remain within approved license scope, timely escalation of material changes or issues
- Client satisfaction - Improved client feedback, successful service reviews, reduced complaints, strong relationship health
- Implementation delivery - On-time client onboarding, reduced launch delays, clear issue tracking, smooth go-live support
- Issue resolution - Faster resolution times, reduced aged issues, effective escalation management, lower repeat incidents
- Control discipline - Strong documentation, audit-ready records, effective SOPs, clear governance evidence
- Operational excellence - Reduced manual interventions, improved process consistency, better dashboards and reporting
- Stakeholder confidence - Positive feedback from Principal Officer, Sales, Compliance, Risk, Legal, Product, and Client Services teams

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:
- 8–12+ years of experience in compliance, client services, client implementation, operations, risk, payments, banking, fintech, financial services, or a related regulated environment.
- Experience supporting financial institutions, banks, payment service providers, fintechs, enterprise clients, or regulated entities.
- Strong understanding of compliance, governance, documentation standards, operational controls, issue management, and audit readiness.
- Demonstrated ability to manage client-facing service responsibilities while maintaining strong regulatory and control discipline.
- Experience coordinating cross-functional work across Sales, Product, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Finance, Technology, Operations, and Client Services.
- Strong project management and implementation coordination skills, including action tracking, dependency management, escalation management, and executive reporting.
- Strong analytical capability and comfort using dashboards, reporting tools, CRM systems, service management tools, and Microsoft Office applications.
- Proven ability to translate complex operational or regulatory requirements into practical processes, checklists, SOPs, and client guidance.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with ability to engage senior internal and external stakeholders.
- High integrity, professionalism, sound judgment, attention to detail, and ability to remain effective under pressure.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Prior experience in payments, card networks, digital payments, cross-border payments, acquiring, issuing, processing, fintech platforms, or payment infrastructure.
- Familiarity with GIFT City, IFSCA, IFSC-regulated entities, ancillary services, financial services regulation, or offshore financial center operations.
- Experience acting as or supporting a Compliance Officer, Nodal Officer, MLRO, branch compliance lead, risk/control lead, or regulated entity governance role.
- Experience with client onboarding, certification, implementation, technical support, service reviews, and operational readiness for financial services products.
- Experience in regulatory reporting, compliance monitoring, internal audits, control testing, governance forums, and policy implementation.
- Ability to manage ambiguity in a growing business environment and build processes from the ground up.
- Strong stakeholder network or working familiarity with banks, PSPs, fintechs, and financial institutions operating in or around GIFT City.
- Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, commerce, law, economics, engineering, technology, or a related discipline.
- Professional certifications in compliance, risk, payments, project management, audit, or financial services operations would be advantageous.

Leadership Capabilities:
The ideal candidate will demonstrate:
- Compliance mindset — ability to interpret obligations, track deliverables, maintain evidence, and escalate issues appropriately.
- Client centricity — commitment to delivering a high-quality service experience for GIFT City clients.
- Operational rigor — strong command of process, documentation, governance, controls, dashboards, and follow-through.
- Issue ownership — ability to drive resolution across multiple internal teams and communicate clearly with clients.
- Cross-functional influence — ability to work effectively across Sales, Product, Legal, Risk, Finance, Technology, and Client Services.
- Judgment and integrity — ability to balance client needs, business objectives, regulatory requirements, and Visa’s reputation.
- Structured execution — ability to manage competing priorities, deadlines, implementations, escalations, and compliance obligations.
- Continuous improvement — willingness to simplify processes, improve controls, and enhance service delivery over time.

Candidate Profile:
This role is best suited for a Senior Manager-level professional with experience in payments, banking, fintech, client services, compliance, operations, or risk. The candidate should be comfortable operating in a regulated environment while also being highly client-facing and execution-oriented.
They should be able to support Visa’s GIFT City regulatory obligations, manage client service delivery, coordinate implementation and issue resolution, and build scalable operating processes for a growing business. The ideal candidate will be detail-oriented, commercially aware, service-minded, and confident working with senior clients and internal stakeholders.

jobs.description:
About Us
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

Job Description

We are seeking a Risk Analyst to support the implementation of risk controls, exposure monitoring routines, collateral arrangements, and KPIs for participants in the payment arrangement, with a particular focus on Issuers.
This professional will play an important role in strengthening the company’s risk mitigation processes by supporting the implementation and ongoing monitoring of financial, operational, exposure, and collateral-related controls. The role will be responsible for monitoring the sufficiency, formalization, and validity of guarantees; tracking participants’ exposure and related KPIs; supporting contract management; preparing management reports and executive presentations; and ensuring an efficient flow of information with clients, Issuers, internal teams, and other relevant stakeholders.
The position requires an analytical mindset, strong organizational skills, the ability to interact with multiple stakeholders, and the capability to transform data and information into structured analyses, risk indicators, and executive materials that support decision-making from a Risk Management perspective.

Essential Functions

- Monitor collateral structures linked to clients and counterparties including bank statements, and systems, tracking sufficiency, eligibility, maturity dates, formalization, adherence to internal policies, and related risk indicators.
- Control and monitor collateral agreements, ensuring they are up to date, properly formalized, and compliant with regulatory and internal requirements.
- Manage the collateral lifecycle, including creation, renewal, replacement, reinforcement, release, and enforcement, when applicable, ensuring proper documentation, governance, and traceability throughout the process.
- Implement, monitor, and continuously enhance KPIs related to collateral, exposure, guarantees, portfolio behavior, operational performance, and risk mitigation effectiveness, maximizing the use of Artificial Intelligence tools to automate analyses, identify patterns, generate insights, and improve the efficiency and accuracy of monitoring routines.
- Prepare periodic reports and management presentations with risk indicators, guarantee positions, relevant exposures, maturity dates, KPI performance, trends, early warning signals, and key areas of attention to support governance and decision-making.
- Consolidate and analyze financial and operational information to identify potential risk deterioration, needs for additional collateral, deviations from defined parameters, or changes in participant behavior, leveraging AI-based tools and analytical models whenever applicable to enhance predictive capacity and monitoring effectiveness.
- Maintain the flow of information with clients by submitting requests, following up, and collecting documents, collateral, and other information required for the monitoring process, ensuring timely updates and completeness of information.
- Interact with internal areas such as Risk, Sales, Legal, Compliance, Operations, and Finance to align information, address contractual matters, implement mitigating actions, and support the evolution of monitoring processes and risk controls.
- Support the development, automation, and maintenance of controls, dashboards, and monitoring indicators, contributing to a preventive, data-driven, and structured view of the portfolio, with a strong focus on maximizing the use of Artificial Intelligence for KPI implementation, anomaly detection, trend analysis, workflow optimization, and executive reporting.
- Support internal and external audits, as well as regulatory requests, by organizing information, evidence, dashboards, reports, and documentation related to contracts and guarantee structures.
- Identify opportunities to apply Artificial Intelligence and automation in risk monitoring routines, including data consolidation, exception handling, alerts, prioritization of critical cases, report generation, and continuous improvement of collateral and exposure monitoring processes.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications
·        Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Risk Management, Engineering, Information System or a related field.
·        Minimum of 3 years of experience working in finance, risk or related areas.
·        Proficiency in the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital tools to increase productivity, support analyses, review information, structure presentations, and optimize recurring activities.
·        Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and control mindset.
·        Excellent communication skills and ability to manage multiple stakeholders.
·        Experience interacting with clients and internal teams to follow up on pending items and manage information flows.
·        Proficiency in Microsoft Office

Preferred Qualifications
·        Experience in Issuer, Acquirer, Processor or Register companies.
·        Knowledge of the four-party model.
·        Knowledge of collateral instruments such as bonds, receivables, escrow accounts, or other financial collateral.
·        Experience with risk control, contract, or collateral management systems.
·        Knowledge of regulations applicable to the financial and payments environment.
·        Be analytical, organized, accurate and detail-oriented with fact-based discipline
·        Fluent, both written and verbal, in Portuguese and English.

Visa is an EEO Employer

Job Description

Team Summary

The AP Digital Sales team is responsible for accelerating Visa’s growth across digital-native clients, fintechs, payment platforms, enablers, issuers, and emerging payment ecosystems. The team builds scalable sales motions that help high-potential clients launch, grow, and optimize payment solutions using Visa’s network, products, data, and value-added services. Working across Asia Pacific, the team partners closely with country, cluster, Product, Client Services, Marketing, Risk, Legal, Finance, and Deal Desk teams to translate market opportunities into repeatable commercial outcomes.

What a Sales Manager, Greater China Region (GCR), Digital Sales does at Visa:

As a sales manager, you will lead a team of Digital Sales Representatives (DSRs) selling to a breadth of clients across assigned segments in GCR. You will define the market and territory coverage strategy, prioritize high-potential opportunities, and build scalable digital sales motions that accelerate client acquisition, portfolio growth, and revenue delivery.

This is a builder and change leadership role that combines people leadership, GCR market development, territory strategy, digital-first sales execution, and cross-functional orchestration. You will help country and regional stakeholders adopt scalable digital sales motions, operating models, strategies, processes, and tools while creating repeatable sales plays across diverse client types and markets within GCR.

Key Responsibilities:

GCR Market Strategy & Development

- Define and execute the Digital Sales growth and territory coverage strategy for GCR across priority markets, assigned segments, and Tier 3 clients.

- Build market maps and segmentation models across all relevant client types, including financial institutions, issuers, acquirers, merchants, fintechs, digital-native businesses, payment platforms, enablers, government entities, and other emerging segments.

- Use data, segmentation, whitespace analysis, client signals, and market potential to identify and prioritize high-potential prospects and existing clients based on addressable opportunity, payment volume potential, strategic fit, product readiness, and ease of execution.

- Translate GCR market dynamics, regulatory considerations, competitive signals, client needs, and partner ecosystems into actionable growth priorities.

Team Leadership & Talent Development

- Lead, coach, and develop a team of Digital Sales Representatives selling to a breadth of clients across assigned segments in GCR.

- Build a high-performance culture through coaching, performance management, talent development, and continuous feedback.

- Attract, onboard, and retain top sales talent while supporting career growth and succession planning.

- Establish a strong sales operating rhythm, including regular training and development, pipeline inspection, deal reviews, coaching cadence, performance management, CRM hygiene, and data-driven decision-making.

Sales Execution & Growth

- Drive new logo acquisition, client expansion, cross-sell, and upsell opportunities across Visa’s network capabilities, issuing and acquiring solutions, commercial payments, tokenization, risk and fraud solutions, cross-border money movement, and value-added services.

- Lead the team's engagement with clients across the full growth journey, from new market entrants and emerging businesses to established financial institutions, merchants, enterprises, and scaled platforms.

- Support complex commercial discussions and strategic partnerships across financial institutions, merchants, fintechs, digital issuers, payment platforms, enablers, processors, government entities, and other priority clients in GCR.

- Coach DSRs on full-cycle sales execution, including prospecting, qualification, solution selling, negotiation, and deal closure.

- Own team-level revenue delivery, pipeline generation, sales productivity, forecast accuracy, conversion performance, and disciplined execution against growth objectives across assigned segments and markets.

- Review and refine sales plays, deal strategies, territory plans, enablement materials, and operating rhythms to improve prospecting, qualification, conversion, activation, and expansion across GCR

Portfolio & Territory Management

- Oversee a large, high-volume territory and portfolio spanning multiple client segments, ensuring effective prioritization and resource allocation.

- Develop data-driven territory and coverage models for Tier 3 clients that balance new client acquisition, expansion of existing relationships, whitespace opportunities, partner-led routes to market, and scalable digital engagement.

- Monitor customer, competitive, and industry trends to identify growth opportunities and emerging market needs

Forecasting & Business Performance

- Drive forecast accuracy and sales discipline through effective use of CRM, reporting, and analytics tools.

- Use data, client signals, sales analytics, automation, AI-enabled tools, and platforms such as Power BI, Tableau, and MSD to identify opportunities, improve prioritization, and increase seller productivity.

- Provide regular business reviews and performance updates to leadership, including risks, opportunities, and strategic recommendations.

Cross-Functional Leadership

- Partner closely with Business Development, Marketing, Product, Value-Added Services, Commercial and Money Movement Solutions, Client Services, Risk, Legal, Finance, Deal Desk, Compliance, and GCR

- country teams to convert demand into qualified opportunities, improve marketing-qualified-lead-to-sales conversion, shape client-relevant propositions, and accelerate commercial outcomes.

- · Act as a change agent with GCR market, country, cluster, and regional leadership to support adoption of the digital operating model, scalable sales motions, strategies, tools, and processes, while maintaining a continuous feedback loop on team contribution and market needs.

- · Influence senior stakeholders without direct authority and provide meaningful recommendations on regional improvements, processes, tools, sales plays, and strategy enhancements.

- · Support the development and rollout of regional go-to-market initiatives, product launches, and strategic growth programs.

What success looks like

- A clear GCR segmentation and data-informed territory coverage strategy is in place across priority markets, assigned segments, and Tier 3 clients.

- A qualified pipeline of high-potential opportunities is built across new logos, expansion accounts, all priority client types, and partner-led routes to market.

- Repeatable sales plays and scalable digital engagement motions are launched, refined, and adopted across GCR markets.

- Revenue delivery, pipeline generation, conversion, forecast accuracy, sales productivity, CRM discipline, and client activation improve across the GCR portfolio.

- Visa's relevance across GCR client segments increases through stronger solution alignment, consultative selling, and adoption of Visa products and value-added services.

Additional Information

- Working location: This role is based in Singapore full-time in the office.

- Travel Requirements: This position requires travel less than 10% of the time.

Why this is important to Visa

This role is critical to making Visa the partner of choice across GCR. By building a market focused Digital Sales growth engine, this manager will:

- Accelerate client acquisition and portfolio growth across financial institutions, merchants, fintechs, digital-native businesses, payment platforms, government entities, and other priority segments.

- Expand adoption of Visa's payment solutions, including card issuance, commercial payments, tokenization, cross-border payments, and value-added services.

- Build scalable sales practices, playbooks, and digital-first engagement motions that can be replicated across GCR markets and client segments.

- Strengthen Visa's position as the partner of choice for clients across GCR.

- Drive sustainable revenue growth and market expansion across a diversified client portfolio.

Qualifications

What you will need:

- Minimum 8+ years of experience in B2B sales, with a proven track record of leading, coaching, and developing high-performing sales teams.
- Experience working with , selling to, or managing relationships with fintechs, digital issuers, payment service providers, financial institutions, or technology companies.
- Strong understanding of the fintech ecosystem, digital payments landscape, and emerging payment trends.
- Strong expertise in digital selling, prospecting, pipeline management, territory planning, and sales execution.
- Prior experience in a full-cycle sales role with direct customer-facing responsibilities.
- Demonstrated ability to leverage data, metrics, and analytics to drive decision-making, forecasting, and business performance.
- Proven success leading teams through change and driving adoption of new tools, processes, and go-to-market strategies.
- Strong commercial acumen with the ability to develop and execute market strategies informed by customer, market, and competitive insights.
- Excellent communication, presentation, and coaching skills, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders across multiple levels i n a highly matrixed organization.
- Ability to inspire, motivate, and develop teams while fostering a high-performance and inclusive culture.
- Demonstrates sound judgment, strategic thinking, and the ability to operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy.

What will also help:

- Familiarity with consultative sales methodologies such as BANT, MEDDIC, Challenger, SPIN, or similar frameworks.
- Additional language capabilities relevant to Asia Pacific markets are preferred.

Visa is an EEO Employer
